newsitem.title: INDIA: India and China sign shipping pact.
newsitem.headline: India and China sign shipping pact.

text.p: India and China on Friday signed a shipping pact extending most favoured nation trading status to each other's vessels in their respective ports, India's Foreign Ministry said in a statement.
"This agreement is an important step in the direction of putting in place an institutional framework for trade and economic interaction between India and China," the foreign ministry said.

Indian Surface Transport Minister T.G. Venkatraman signed a maritime transport agreement with Chinese Foreign Minister Qian Qichen, who is accompanying his country's President Jiang Zemin on a visit to India, the ministry said.

The agreement will streamline formalities for vessels' entries and departures, port usage for loading and unloading cargo, payment of port dues and charges, and the use of navigation services and facilities, the ministry said.
Under the agreement, all income from shipping enterprises in both countries will be settled in freely convertible, mutually acceptable currencies.
The two nations also agreed on measures to avoid double taxation of income and profits derived from international maritime transport, the statement added.
